body.h1: Claim Rejections under 35 U.S.C. § 112(b) or 35 U.S.C. § 112 (pre-AIA), Second Paragraph
body.p: The Office Action rejected claims 1-7, 10 and 14-20 under 35 U.S.C. § 112(b) or 35 U.S.C. § 112 (pre-AIA), second paragraph, as being indefinite for failing to particularly point out and distinctly claim the subject matter which the inventor or a joint inventor (or for applications subject to pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 112, the applicant), regards as the invention.

More specifically, claims 1-7 and 14-20 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 112(b) or 35 U.S.C. § 112 (pre-AIA), second paragraph, as being indefinite because of insufficient antecedent basis. Applicant(s) respectfully submit(s) that the foregoing amendments traverse the rejections and claims 1-7 and 14-19 are allowable under 35 U.S.C. § 112, second paragraph. Reconsideration and withdrawal of the rejections are respectfully requested.

In addition, the Office Action rejected claims 3, 10 and 16 under 35 U.S.C. § 112(b) or 35 U.S.C. § 112 (pre-AIA), second paragraph, as being indefinite because of the term "substantially." Applicant(s) respectfully submit(s) that relative terminology is acceptable in claim language if it provides enough certainty to one of skill in the art when read in the context of the invention. M.P.E.P. § 2173.05(b). Paragraph [0081] in the specification states "As used herein, words of approximation such as, without limitation, "about", "substantial" or "substantially" refers to a condition that when so modified is understood to not necessarily be absolute or perfect but would be considered close enough to those of ordinary skill in the art to warrant designating the condition as being present." Accordingly, applicant(s) respectfully submit(s) that the claimed terminology in view of paragraph [0081] provides enough certainty to one of skill in the art when read in the context of the invention. Applicant(s) respectfully submit(s) that claims 3, 10 and 16 are allowable under 35 U.S.C. § 112(b) or 35 U.S.C. § 112 (pre-AIA), second paragraph. Reconsideration and withdrawal of the rejections are respectfully requested.
The Office Action rejected claims 1-4, 6, 8-11, 13-17 and 19-20 under 35 U.S.C. § 102(a)(1) and (a2)as being anticipated by Milde, Jr. (hereinafter "Milde"), US Patent Number

For anticipation, a single reference must identically disclose every element of the claimed invention. Corning Glass Works v. Sumitomo Electric, 9 USPQ 2d 1962, 1965 (Fed. Cir. 1989). A reference that excludes a claimed element, no matter how insubstantial or obvious, is enough to negate anticipation. Connell v. Sears, Roebuck & Co., 220 USPQ 193, 198 (Fed. Cir. 1983).

Applicant(s) respectfully submit that claims 1-4, 6, 8-11, 13-17 and 19 are not anticipated by Milde and are, therefore, allowable under 35 U.S.C. § 102(a)(1) and (a2) for the reasons stated below. Reconsideration and withdrawal of the rejections are respectfully requested.
Claims 1, 8 and 14

The Office Action stated that "the left and right hand portion of element 14" in Figure 1 of Milde discloses a first wing segment and a second wing segment. (pages 4-5). Applicant(s) respectfully disagree(s) because Milde discloses a "wingless personal air transport" (Abstract; claim 1), and element 14 is an annular platform (col. 5, lines 23-24) that encloses fuel tanks and "prevent[s] air forced downward by the propellers 20 from recycling upward and entering the driven airstream again" (col. 5, lines 45-52). As a result, applicant(s) respectfully submit(s) that Milde does not identically disclose a first wing segment and a second wing segment as recited in claims 1, 8 and 14.

The Office Action also stated that Milde discloses the nose section of the fuselage extends forward beyond the propellers, the leading edge of the first wing segment and the leading edge of the second wing segment when the aircraft is in forward flight. (page 5). Milde discloses "Joystick 24 is used in its conventional way to orient the craft front to back and side to side. This control

adjusts the relative speeds of the engines to cause the craft to tilt. For example, pushing the joystick forward causes the rearward engines of the craft to increase in speed and (if desired) the front engines to decrease their speed slightly, thereby increasing the relative lift in the back and causing the craft to tilt forward. This forward tilt results in the craft moving forward in the horizontal direction." (col. 6, lines 18-27).

First, applicant(s) respectfully submit(s) that the foregoing portion of Milde does not expressly state or "identically disclose" the craft is capable of tilted flight such that the nose of the fuselage, the clear plastic bubble 12, extends forward beyond the annular platform 14 during such flight. Second, applicant(s) respectfully submit(s) that based on FIG. 2 of Milde, the craft would have to be tilted by more than 60 degrees for the clear plastic bubble 12 to extend forward beyond the annular platform 14. Applicant(s) respectfully submit(s) that Milde's craft is not capable maintaining flight at a tilt angle sufficient for the clear plastic bubble to extend forward beyond the annular platform 14 because: (1) the propellers 20 would not provide sufficient lift during flight at such a tilt angle; and (2) the wingless craft does not have aerodynamic wings to provide lift during flight at such a tilt angle. Applicant(s) respectfully submit(s) that Milde solves this problem by adding small thrusters 112 on opposite sides of the craft to speed the craft in the forward or reverse direction. (column 9, lines 33-40; FIGS. 21-22). As a result, applicant(s) respectfully submit(s) that Milde does not identically disclose "the nose section of the fuselage extends forward beyond the propellers, the leading edge of the first wing segment and the leading edge of the second wing segment when the aircraft is in forward flight" as recited in claims 1, 8 and 14.

For at least the foregoing reasons, applicant(s) respectfully submit(s) that Milde does not identically disclose each and every element of claims 1, 8 and 14. Claims 1, 8 and 14 are, therefore, allowable under 35 U.S.C. § 102. Reconsideration and withdrawal of the rejections are respectfully requested.

Applicant(s) respectfully submit(s) that the deficiencies detailed above in reference to the cited reference are sufficient to traverse the rejections. As a result, any additional distinctions between the claims and the cited reference are unnecessary and applicant(s) reserve(s) the right to present additional arguments against the statements and characterizations stated in the Office Action, and the cited reference in the event the rejections are not withdrawn.
